verses.text: We thank God always concerning all of you, making mention of you in our prayers,
verses.marked_text: We thank God always concerning all of you, making mention of you in our prayers,

verses.text: Remembering unceasingly your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father;
verses.marked_text: Remembering unceasingly your work of faith and labor of love and endurance of hope in our Lord Jesus Christ, before our God and Father;

verses.text: Knowing , brothers, beloved of God, your selection ;
verses.marked_text: Knowing , brothers, beloved of God, your selection ;

verses.text: For our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and in much assurance, even as you know what kind of men we were among you for your sake.
verses.marked_text: For our gospel did not come to you in word only, but also in power and in the Holy Spirit and in much assurance, even as you know what kind of men we were among you for your sake.

verses.text: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with joy of the Holy Spirit,
verses.marked_text: And you became imitators of us and of the Lord, having received the word in much affliction with joy of the Holy Spirit,

verses.text: So that you became a pattern to all those who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.
verses.marked_text: So that you became a pattern to all those who believe in Macedonia and in Achaia.

verses.text: For from you the word of the Lord has sounded out; not only in Macedonia and in Achaia, but in every place, your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need of saying anything.
verses.marked_text: For from you the word of the Lord has sounded out; not only in Macedonia and in Achaia, but in every place, your faith toward God has gone out, so that we have no need of saying anything.

verses.text: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of entrance we had toward you and how you turned to God from the idols to serve a living and true God,
verses.marked_text: For they themselves report concerning us what kind of entrance we had toward you and how you turned to God from the idols to serve a living and true God,

verses.text: And await His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead, Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath which is coming.
verses.marked_text: And await His Son from the heavens, whom He raised from the dead, Jesus, who delivers us from the wrath which is coming.

footnotes.text: Thessalonica was a city of the Roman Empire, in the province of Macedonia, which was north of the province of Achaia. It was the next city the apostle Paul and his co-worker Silvanus visited after Philippi, after the Macedonian call he received on his second ministry journey ( Acts 16:9-12 ; 17:1-4 ). The apostle stayed and worked in Thessalonica for only a short time, probably less than one month ( Acts 17:2 ).

In this chapter the Triune God is revealed in His triune work upon us — the Father selected us ( vv. 1 , 3-4 ), the Son delivers us ( v. 10 ), and the Holy Spirit propagates, imparts, and transmits the Triune God into us ( vv. 5-6 ). Such a triune work is for our enjoyment of His salvation.
The Greek word denotes acts, actions, activities.
Or, toil, endeavoring, striving, working.
I.e., endurance issuing from hoping in our Lord Jesus Christ.

The word preached by Paul was the embodiment of the Triune God, conveying and transmitting Him — the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit — into the believers in Christ. This word as the divine gospel was received by the Thessalonians, who were typical Gentile unbelievers.
Implying a receptive welcome.

outlines.text: 1. The care of a nursing mother and an exhorting father (vv. 1-12)

verses.text: For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance toward you, that it has not been in vain.
verses.marked_text: For you yourselves know, brothers, our entrance toward you, that it has not been in vain.
outlines: 1. The care of a nursing mother and an exhorting father (vv. 1-12)

verses.text: But having suffered previously and having been outrageously treated, even as you know, in Philippi , we were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much struggle.
verses.marked_text: But having suffered previously and having been outrageously treated, even as you know, in Philippi , we were bold in our God to speak to you the gospel of God in much struggle.

verses.text: For our exhortation is not out of deception nor out of uncleanness nor in guile;
verses.marked_text: For our exhortation is not out of deception nor out of uncleanness nor in guile;

verses.text: But even as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing men but God, who proves our hearts.
verses.marked_text: But even as we have been approved by God to be entrusted with the gospel, so we speak, not as pleasing men but God, who proves our hearts.

verses.text: For neither were we found at any time with flattering speech, even as you know, nor with a pretext for covetousness; God is witness.
verses.marked_text: For neither were we found at any time with flattering speech, even as you know, nor with a pretext for covetousness; God is witness.

verses.text: Nor did we seek glory from men, neither from you nor from others, though we could have stood on our authority as apostles of Christ.
verses.marked_text: Nor did we seek glory from men, neither from you nor from others, though we could have stood on our authority as apostles of Christ.

verses.text: But we were gentle in your midst, as a nursing mother would cherish her own children.
verses.marked_text: But we were gentle in your midst, as a nursing mother would cherish her own children.

verses.text: Yearning in this way over you, we were well pleased to impart to you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls, because you became beloved to us.
verses.marked_text: Yearning in this way over you, we were well pleased to impart to you not only the gospel of God but also our own souls, because you became beloved to us.

verses.text: For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail: While working night and day so as not to be burdensome to any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.
verses.marked_text: For you remember, brothers, our labor and travail: While working night and day so as not to be burdensome to any of you, we proclaimed to you the gospel of God.

verses.text: You are witnesses, as well as God, how in a holy and righteous and blameless manner we conducted ourselves toward you who believe,
verses.marked_text: You are witnesses, as well as God, how in a holy and righteous and blameless manner we conducted ourselves toward you who believe,

verses.text: Just as you know how we were to each one of you, as a father to his own children, exhorting you and consoling you and testifying,
verses.marked_text: Just as you know how we were to each one of you, as a father to his own children, exhorting you and consoling you and testifying,

verses.text: So that you might walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory .
verses.marked_text: So that you might walk in a manner worthy of God, who calls you into His own kingdom and glory .

verses.text: And because of this we also thank God unceasingly that when you received the word of God, which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but even as it truly is, the word of God, which also operates in you who believe.
verses.marked_text: And because of this we also thank God unceasingly that when you received the word of God, which you heard from us, you accepted it not as the word of men but even as it truly is, the word of God, which also operates in you who believe.

verses.text: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus, for you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, even as they also from the Jews,
verses.marked_text: For you, brothers, became imitators of the churches of God which are in Judea in Christ Jesus, for you also suffered the same things from your own countrymen, even as they also from the Jews,

verses.text: Who both killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets and drove us out; and they are not pleasing to God and are contrary to all men,
verses.marked_text: Who both killed the Lord Jesus and the prophets and drove us out; and they are not pleasing to God and are contrary to all men,

verses.text: In that they forbid us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, so that they fill up their sins always. But wrath has come upon them to the uttermost .
verses.marked_text: In that they forbid us to speak to the Gentiles that they may be saved, so that they fill up their sins always. But wrath has come upon them to the uttermost .

verses.text: But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a little while, in presence, not in heart, were more abundantly eager with great desire to see your face.
verses.marked_text: But we, brothers, having been bereaved of you for a little while, in presence, not in heart, were more abundantly eager with great desire to see your face.

verses.text: Therefore we wanted to come to you, indeed I Paul, both once and again, yet Satan hindered us.
verses.marked_text: Therefore we wanted to come to you, indeed I Paul, both once and again, yet Satan hindered us.

verses.text: For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at His coming ? Are not even you?
verses.marked_text: For what is our hope or joy or crown of boasting before our Lord Jesus at His coming ? Are not even you?

verses.text: For you are our glory and joy.
verses.marked_text: For you are our glory and joy.

footnotes.text: The apostle stressed repeatedly their entrance toward the believers ( 1 Thes. 1:5 , 9 ). This shows that their manner of life played a great role in infusing the gospel into the new converts. It was not only what they said but what they were.
This was the apostles' experience of God in enjoying Him as their boldness in the struggle for the gospel.

Or, pretense, cloak. To have any pretext for covetousness is to peddle or adulterate the word of God ( 2 Cor. 2:17 ; 4:2 ). It is also to pretend to be godly for the sake of gain ( 1 Tim. 6:5 ; Titus 1:11 ; 2 Pet. 2:3 ).
To seek glory from men is a real temptation to every Christian worker. Many have been devoured and spoiled by this matter.

Or, asserted authority. Lit., been able to be in weight; i.e., been burdensome (cf. v. 9 ; 1 Cor. 9:4-12 ). To assert authority, dignity, or right in Christian work damages that work. The Lord Jesus, while on earth, gave up His dignity ( John 13:4-5 ), and the apostle preferred not to use his right ( 1 Cor. 9:12 ).
See note Luke 1:75 1a . Holy refers to conduct toward God, righteous to conduct toward men, and blameless to conduct toward all — God, men, and Satan.
The apostle was strong in stressing what or how they were ( 1 Thes. 1:5 ), because what they were opened the way to bring their new converts into God's full salvation.
Lit., the word of hearing of God from us.
The word received by the believers was from the apostles, but it was of God. Its source, its origin, was God and not the apostles.
Since the word of God is living and operative ( Heb. 4:12 ), it operates in the believing ones.
Lit., to the end; hence, to the uttermost.
This word implies that the apostles considered the new converts precious and dear to them. Paul likened their departure from them to a bereavement, a loss that they suffered through missing them.
Lit., the season of an hour.
This is the apostles' yearning over the new converts ( v. 8 ).
Because the apostles were carrying out the will of God, Satan frustrated them.
Since the apostles were the believers' nursing mother and exhorting father ( vv. 7 , 11 ), the believers, as the apostles' children, were their glory and joy.

verses.text: Therefore when we could bear it no longer, we thought it good to be left in Athens alone,
verses.marked_text: Therefore when we could bear it no longer, we thought it good to be left in Athens alone,

verses.text: And we sent Timothy, our brother and God 's fellow worker in the gospel of Christ, to establish and encourage you for the sake of your faith,
verses.marked_text: And we sent Timothy, our brother and God 's fellow worker in the gospel of Christ, to establish and encourage you for the sake of your faith,

verses.text: That no one would be shaken by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.
verses.marked_text: That no one would be shaken by these afflictions; for you yourselves know that we are appointed for this.

verses.text: For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we are to be afflicted, even as it also came to pass and you know.
verses.marked_text: For even when we were with you, we told you beforehand that we are to be afflicted, even as it also came to pass and you know.

verses.text: Because of this, when I also could bear it no longer, I sent to find out concerning your faith, lest perhaps the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.
verses.marked_text: Because of this, when I also could bear it no longer, I sent to find out concerning your faith, lest perhaps the tempter had tempted you and our labor would be in vain.

verses.text: But Timothy, having just come to us from you and announcing the good news to us of your faith and love and that you have kind remembrance of us always and long to see us, just as we also you,
verses.marked_text: But Timothy, having just come to us from you and announcing the good news to us of your faith and love and that you have kind remembrance of us always and long to see us, just as we also you,

verses.text: Because of this we were comforted because of you, brothers, in all our necessity and affliction, through your faith;
verses.marked_text: Because of this we were comforted because of you, brothers, in all our necessity and affliction, through your faith;

verses.text: Because now we live if you stand firm in the Lord.
verses.marked_text: Because now we live if you stand firm in the Lord.

verses.text: For what thanks can we return to God concerning you for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,
verses.marked_text: For what thanks can we return to God concerning you for all the joy with which we rejoice because of you before our God,

verses.text: Night and day petitioning exceedingly so that we may see your face and complete the things that are lacking in your faith?
verses.marked_text: Night and day petitioning exceedingly so that we may see your face and complete the things that are lacking in your faith?

verses.text: Now may our God and Father Himself and our Lord Jesus make straight our path to you;
verses.marked_text: Now may our God and Father Himself and our Lord Jesus make straight our path to you;

verses.text: And the Lord cause you to increase and abound in love to one another and to all, just as we also to you,
verses.marked_text: And the Lord cause you to increase and abound in love to one another and to all, just as we also to you,

verses.text: So that He may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints .
verses.marked_text: So that He may establish your hearts blameless in holiness before our God and Father at the coming of our Lord Jesus with all His saints .

footnotes.text: Some MSS read, minister of God. A minister of God is God's fellow worker ( 1 Cor. 3:9 ; 2 Cor. 6:1 ). What a privilege! What a blessing!
Or, exhort, comfort.

If we are established in the faith ( v. 2 ), afflictions will work out for our good ( Rom. 8:28 ) according to God's purpose in His appointment. Otherwise, we may be shaken by the tempter ( v. 5 ) through the afflictions.
Imperfect tense, indicating repeated action.
The apostle was in Corinth after leaving Athens ( Acts 17:15-16 ; 18:1 , 5 ). It was in Corinth that he wrote this lovely letter to the dear saints in Thessalonica for their encouragement.
Or, distress. See note 1 Cor. 7:26 2 and note 2 Cor. 12:10 3b .
The believers' standing firm in the Lord ministers life to the apostles.

Or, perfect. The verb form of the Greek word in 2 Cor. 13:9 (see note 2 Cor. 13:9 2b ). The believers in Thessalonica, being young in the Lord, were still lacking in their new faith. The apostle realized this with much loving concern for them. This was his reason for writing this Epistle.

The establishing of the believers' hearts blameless issues from faith and love, as mentioned in the preceding verses. This spontaneously produces the hope of the coming back of our dear Lord, in whom we believe and whom we love. Hence, again we see that faith, love, and hope are the implied factors in the construction of this Epistle.

Inwardly, our heart must be established in holiness; outwardly, our body must be preserved in sanctification ( 1 Thes. 4:4 ; 5:23 ). This is so that we may have a holy life, and this holy life is for the church life.
Believers in Christ (see note Rom. 1:2 3 and note 1 Cor. 1:2 6d ), including the Old Testament saints ( Dan. 7:18 , 21-22 , 25 , 27 ; Zech. 14:5 ).

verses.text: Therefore comfort one another with these words.
verses.marked_text: Therefore comfort one another with these words.

footnotes.text: Implying to keep, to preserve.

Concerning the interpretation of vessel here, there are two schools: one holds that the vessel is man's body, as in 2 Cor. 4:7 ; the other, that it is a man's wife, as in 1 Pet. 3:7 . The context of this verse and the next verse, which include phrases such as each one of you, in sanctification and honor, and especially not in the passion of lust, justifies the interpretation of the first school but not that of the second. Here the apostle considered man's body his vessel, just as David did in 1 Sam. 21:5 . In the same matter concerning the use of the body, both Paul and David considered man's body his vessel. To keep, or preserve, man's vessel in sanctification and honor, not allowing it to indulge in the passion of lust, is the safeguard against committing fornication.

Sanctification refers more to a holy condition before God; honor, to a respectable standing before man. Man was created for God's purpose with a high standing, and marriage was ordained by God for the propagation of man to fulfill God's purpose. Hence, marriage should be held in honor ( Heb. 13:4 ). To abstain from fornication is not only to remain in a sanctified condition before God but also to hold and keep a standing of honor before man.
I.e., overpass (limits), overreach, transgress, go beyond. Overstep and take advantage of his brother refers to the committing of adultery with a brother's wife.
Or, make a gain of; hence, defraud.
The matter of fornication, mentioned in v. 3 .
Things such as overstepping and taking advantage of others.
Lit., based on.
I.e., in the element of sanctification, in the sphere of God's holy nature.
This verse is the conclusion of the section that begins with v. 3 .
I.e., rejects the charge in the preceding verses.
Gk. philadelphia, composed of phileo, to love (referring to love in general, as to have affection for ), and adelphos, brother.
I.e., dead ( v. 16 ; John 11:11-14 ; 1 Cor. 11:30 ). For believers to die was considered by both the Lord and the apostle as going to sleep.

In Rev. 12 the man-child, i.e., the overcomers, is caught up, raptured, to the throne of God in the third heaven before the great tribulation, the last three and a half years of the present age ( Rev. 12:5-6 , 14 ). Here, the majority of the believers, including those who are resurrected from the dead and those who are living at that time, are raptured to the air at the end of the great tribulation, at the time of the Lord's coming (parousia).

verses.text: The grace of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you.

footnotes.text: This indicates that the day of the Lord's coming is kept secret and will come suddenly, being known beforehand by no one ( Matt. 24:42-43 ; Rev. 3:3 ; 16:15 ).
This is the result of men's intense rebellion against God under Satan's instigation near the time of the Lord's coming ( v. 2 ).
The hope of our Lord's coming back ( 1 Thes. 1:3 ), which will be our salvation from both the coming destruction ( v. 3 ) and the slavery of corruption of the old creation ( Rom. 8:21-25 ).
Not salvation from eternal perdition through the Lord's death, but salvation from the coming destruction ( v. 3 ) through the Lord's coming back.
Since God did not appoint us to wrath, we should watch, be sober, and fight ( vv. 6 , 8 ) to cooperate with God that we may obtain His salvation through the Lord Jesus.
Or, are awake. I.e., are alive.
I.e., are dead ( 1 Thes. 4:13-15 ).
On the one hand, the Lord is away from us and we are awaiting His coming back; on the other hand, He is with us ( Matt. 28:20 ) and we can live together with Him ( Rom. 6:8 ).
The apostle was probably referring here to the elders who labor in teaching and take the lead among the believers ( 1 Tim. 5:17 ).

To take the lead is not mainly to rule but to set an example in doing things first, that others may follow. The elders not only should labor in teaching but also should do things as an example. The example may become a ground for their admonishing.
To regard the leading ones and to be at peace with one another is the proper condition of a local church.
This means that regardless of how others treat us, even if their treatment is evil, we should pursue what is good for them.
This is based on the conditions mentioned in vv. 14-15 .
This is to have uninterrupted fellowship with God in our spirit. It requires perseverance ( Rom. 12:12 ; Col. 4:2 ) with a strong spirit ( Eph. 6:18 ).
Because all things work together for our good that we may be transformed and conformed to the image of Christ ( Rom. 8:28-29 ).
This clause modifies the three preceding exhortations. God wants us to live a rejoicing, praying, and thanking life. Such a life is a glory to God and a shame to His enemy.
The Spirit causes our spirit to be burning ( Rom. 12:11 ) and our gifts to be flaming ( 2 Tim. 1:6 ). Hence, we should not quench Him.
Count as nothing, lightly esteem.
I.e., prophesying, the prophetic speech that issues from a revelation. It does not need to be a prediction (see 1 Cor. 14:1 , 3-4 and notes there).

Including to discern prophecies ( 1 Cor. 14:29 ), to discern the spirits ( 1 Cor. 12:10 ), to test the spirits ( 1 John 4:1 ), to prove what is the will of God ( Rom. 12:2 ), and to prove what is well pleasing to the Lord ( Eph. 5:10 ).

The Greek word means species. It denotes anything in view, anything in perception; hence, a sight. It refers not to the appearance of evil but to the kind, the form, the shape, the sight, of evil. The believers, who live a holy life in faith, love, and hope, should abstain from evil of any kind.

And conjoins the blessing of God's sanctifying of our entire being, given in this verse, and the charge to abstain from every kind of evil, given in the preceding verse. On the one hand, we abstain from every kind of evil; on the other hand, God sanctifies us wholly. We cooperate with God that we may have a holy living.
The God of peace is the Sanctifier; His sanctification brings in peace. When we are wholly sanctified by Him from within, we have peace with Him and with man in every way ( v. 13 ).
Or, entirely, thoroughly, to the consummation. God sanctifies us wholly, so that no part of our being, of either our spirit or soul or body, will be left common or profane.

God not only sanctifies us wholly but also preserves our spirit, soul, and body complete. Wholly is quantitative; complete is qualitative. Quantitatively, God sanctifies us wholly; qualitatively, God preserves us complete, i.e., He keeps our spirit, soul, and body perfect. Through the fall our body was ruined, our soul was contaminated, and our spirit was deadened. In God's full salvation our entire being is saved and made complete and perfect. For this, God is preserving our spirit from any deadening element ( Heb. 9:14 ), our soul from remaining natural and old ( Matt. 16:24-26 ), and our body from the ruin of sin ( 1 Thes. 4:4 ; Rom. 6:6 ). Such a preservation by God and His thorough sanctification sustain us to live a holy life unto maturity that we may meet the Lord in His parousia.
Or, in the presence (parousia).
The faithful God who called us will also sanctify us wholly and preserve our entire being complete.
Some MSS insert holy. This would mean that, since this Epistle is concerned with the holy life of the believers, the apostle in his concluding charge called the believers "the holy brothers."
